item.content:encoded:
Looking to build your knowledge and skills in sustainability, climate action, sustainable development and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)? The United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) offers a range of free online courses covering topics including climate change, sustainable development, SDG budgeting, climate negotiations, women’s leadership, official statistics, resilience and the 2030 Agenda.

These free UNITAR courses provide an opportunity for learners, professionals, policymakers, students and development practitioners to strengthen their knowledge and skills in areas that are increasingly important for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

Free UNITAR Sustainability and Sustainable Development Courses

Below is a list of 18 free sustainability courses from UNITAR covering sustainable development, climate action, SDG implementation, data, governance and related topics.

1. Anticipatory Governance: Systems Thinking & Strategic Foresight for SDG-Aligned Integrated Planning

This course explores systems thinking, strategic foresight and anticipatory governance to support integrated planning aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/gw4p_XMB

2. Inclusive Learning Design

Learn about inclusive learning design and approaches that can help make learning environments more accessible and responsive to diverse learners.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/dt8bfH2w

3. Practical Methods to Implement and Uphold the FPOS for Producers

This course focuses on practical approaches to implementing and upholding the Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics (FPOS) for producers of official statistics.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/g5hAWCRz

4. Introduction to Official Statistics

Gain an introduction to official statistics, including their importance for evidence-based policymaking, development planning and informed decision-making.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/gmszNJHX

5. Insurance and the Sustainable Development Goals

Explore the relationship between insurance and the Sustainable Development Goals, including how insurance can contribute to sustainable development and resilience.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/gj5aMhXg

6. Developing Skills for Women Leadership in Climate Action

This course focuses on developing skills to strengthen women’s leadership in climate action and support greater participation in climate-related decision-making.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/eE5saH5D

7. Strengthening Stakeholder Engagement for the Implementation and Review of the 2030 Agenda

Learn approaches for strengthening stakeholder engagement in the implementation and review of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/dw7gix7

8. Introduction to Sports for Climate Action

Discover how the sports sector can contribute to climate action and support broader efforts to address climate change and advance sustainable development.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/eVggDGWj

9. SDG-Aligned Budgeting

Learn about SDG-aligned budgeting and how public budgets can be connected to national sustainable development priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/gHe26r_z

10. Geospatial Information Technology in Fragile Contexts

Explore the use of geospatial information technology in fragile contexts and its potential applications for development, planning and decision-making.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/dFUpd6UR

11. Mainstreaming the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development

This course examines approaches to mainstreaming the 2030 Agenda and integrating sustainable development priorities into policies, plans and development processes.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/dpdj2PEH

12. Art and the Stewardship of the Ocean

Explore the relationship between art, ocean stewardship and sustainable development, highlighting creative approaches to raising awareness about ocean-related challenges.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/eyAuKgv2

13. Infrastructure Asset Management for Sustainable Development

Learn about infrastructure asset management and its importance for sustainable, resilient and effective infrastructure development.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/gxAfSSv4

14. Mastering International Climate Negotiations: All You Need to Know

Develop knowledge of international climate negotiations, including key concepts and processes relevant to global climate policy and action.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/eqUemTwB

15. Environmental SDG Indicators

Learn about environmental indicators for the Sustainable Development Goals and how data and indicators can support sustainable development monitoring and decision-making.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/dMG9U7Nv

16. Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics (FPOS) and Their Relevance for Policymakers

Understand the Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics (FPOS) and their relevance to policymakers, evidence-based policy and effective decision-making.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/dCHDsJaT

17. Strengthening Climate Adaptation and Resilience

This course explores climate adaptation and resilience, helping learners understand approaches to strengthening resilience to climate-related risks and impacts.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/eRFamQcv

18. Understanding Data and Statistics Better – for More Effective SDG Decision Making

Develop a better understanding of data and statistics for SDG decision-making and learn how reliable evidence can support more effective sustainable development policies and actions.

🔗 Course: https://lnkd.in/d9My2QH

Who Can Take These Free UNITAR Courses?

These courses may be particularly useful for:

  • Students and recent graduates
  • Young professionals
  • Development practitioners
  • Sustainability professionals
  • Climate and environmental practitioners
  • Policymakers and government officials
  • Researchers and academics
  • NGO and civil society professionals
  • Professionals working on the SDGs
  • Anyone interested in climate action and sustainable development

Why Take Free UNITAR Online Courses?

UNITAR’s online learning opportunities can help learners develop knowledge relevant to some of the world’s most pressing development challenges. Topics covered across these courses include climate change, sustainability, sustainable development, the SDGs, the 2030 Agenda, climate adaptation, resilience, data and statistics, governance and policy.

For students and professionals, completing relevant online courses can also be a useful way to expand knowledge, develop professional skills and strengthen a CV or professional profile.

Start Learning Online

If you are looking for free online sustainability courses, free UN courses, climate change courses, SDG courses or sustainable development training, explore the UNITAR opportunities above and check the individual course pages for the latest information on eligibility, registration, course dates and completion requirements.

Bookmark this page and share it with students, young professionals and development practitioners who may benefit from these free learning opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the CSC Mentoring Programme 2026-27, offering Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni the opportunity to connect, share knowledge and skills, build professional networks, and support development impact.

The CSC’s Mentoring Programme connects Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni to support knowledge and skills development, and provide practical tools to support Scholars in achieving development impact.

Why Take Part in the CSC Mentoring Programme?

Commonwealth Scholars will have the opportunity to learn from an experienced Commonwealth Alumnus, and gain valuable insights, personalised guidance, and practical advice to help maximise their development impact.

Mentees will also be able to build professional connections, receive support in adapting to life and study in the UK, and develop their professional confidence for future career opportunities.

Commonwealth Alumni play a key role in shaping a new Scholar’s journey and future impact. As Mentors, they will provide advice on developing new skills and knowledge and applying this learning to drive development impact after the scholarship.

The programme offers a rewarding opportunity for Mentors to enhance their mentoring and leadership skills, expand their networks, and share their expertise and experiences within the wider CSC community.

The Mentoring Programme runs for one year from December 2026 until December 2027, with sessions taking place online.

How to Apply for the CSC Mentoring Programme 2026-27

All eligible Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni will receive full information about the programme and how to apply in September 2026.

Application Deadline

The deadline for applications is 23:59 (BST) on Sunday 11 October 2026.

You can find out more about the opportunity and read testimonials from previous participants on the CSC Mentoring Programme page.

For more information about the eligibility criteria, please read the CSC Mentoring Programme – FAQs.

If you have any questions about the CSC Mentoring Programme, or how to apply, please contact alumni@cscuk.org.uk for more information.

CSC Mentoring Programme

The Mentoring Programme enables Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni to connect and inspire each other to create real-world impact.

By matching new Scholars with experienced Alumni working in fields relevant to their studies, the programme offers a unique opportunity for one-on-one guidance and practical insight, helping scholars turn academic knowledge into meaningful action after their Scholarship.

How Does the Programme Work?

Applications open in August each year, with the programme running from the following January – December (one year cycle).

Successful applicants are matched with a Mentor or Mentee whose background and aspirations closely align with their own, ensuring a personalised experience.

Your mentoring partnership will progress through five stages, each designed to help you achieve key milestones and make the most of your time together. You’ll be supported throughout the year with programme handbooks, regular communications, and skills development resources, giving you the tools to succeed at every stage.

To help you get started and build a productive mentoring partnership, you will be invited to join online information sessions at the beginning of the programme. There’ll also be lively virtual meet-ups where you can connect with other Mentees and Mentors, share your experiences, and build best practice.

Who Can Join the CSC Mentoring Programme?

Commonwealth Master’s and Doctoral Scholars

Become a Mentee and unlock the chance to turn your academic achievements into real-world impact. Through personalised guidance from a Commonwealth Alumnus, you’ll learn how to translate your skills and knowledge into tangible development outcomes back home and gain invaluable insights on navigating life and studies in the UK.

As a Mentee, you’ll receive tailored support to help you excel both academically and professionally, with advice on everything from adapting to a new culture to building the employability skills that will set you apart after your Scholarship.

Commonwealth Alumni

By becoming a Mentor, you’ll play a crucial role in guiding and inspiring the next generation of Scholars, helping them to develop the skills and confidence needed to create meaningful change in their home countries and fields.

As a Mentor, you’ll have the rewarding opportunity to share your knowledge and offer practical advice, supporting a Scholar as they navigate their studies and future career. You’ll also expand your own skillset, enhancing your leadership, communication, and mentoring abilities.

You will receive information via email when applications open. If you have any questions, you can read our Frequently Asked Questions page or contact alumni@cscuk.org.uk.

Why Should I Take Part?

To find out what inspired previous Mentors and Mentees to join the programme, read the testimonials below.

“The Mentoring Programme exceeded my expectations in most areas, particularly in understanding how to apply my studies for development impact and learning from my Mentor’s expertise as a Commonwealth Scholar. My Mentor provided invaluable insights into practical applications of my field, helping me align my academic goals with real-world challenges. My Mentor also offered excellent professional development advice, which has been instrumental in shaping my career plans. While the advice on living and studying in the UK was helpful, it aligned closely with what I had anticipated. Overall, the programme has been a transformative experience.”

2023 Mentee from India

Commonwealth Alumni who have significant professional experience post-Scholarship can volunteer to become a Mentor.

As a Mentor, you will have the opportunity to share your expertise to support a new Scholar in developing appropriate skills and knowledge to achieve development impact post-Scholarship and provide advice on how these skills can applied in their home country or home country region. Through the programme, you will develop mentoring and professional skills, such as leadership, communication, and knowledge-sharing.

Image of Commonwealth Scholars discussing

“The CSC Mentoring Programme provided a well-structured platform for personal and professional growth, offering both the resources and guidance necessary to foster meaningful Mentor-Mentee relationships. The programme enabled me to enhance my mentoring skills, while also giving me the opportunity to make a positive impact on my Mentee’s academic, professional, and social development. The collaborative aspect was particularly rewarding, as it allowed me to share knowledge and learn from my Mentee’s fresh perspectives. I feel that the programme successfully met its objectives, and I would recommend it to fellow Alumni seeking to develop as Mentors.”

2023 Mentor from Pakistan

How Does the Programme Work?

Applications open in September 2025 and pairings will be announced in November 2025. The programme runs for one year from December 2025 to December 2026.

Image of Commonwealth Scholars discussing

Successful applicants are matched in a one-to-one mentoring pairing based on their application responses.

The programme consists of 5 stages, which help guide pairs through important milestones to achieve their goals for the programme. Mentees and Mentors will have access to resources including programme handbooks and a range of skills development resources. All participants will have the opportunity to attend virtual information sessions at the start of the programme and virtual meet-up sessions to connect with fellow Mentees and Mentors and share best practice.

How Can I Apply?

All eligible Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni will receive full information about the programme and how to apply in September 2024. You can find out more about the by reading Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

If you have any questions about the programme, contact the CSC Alumni Team at alumni@cscuk.org.uk.

CSC Mentoring Programme Eligibility

Who Can Apply to Take Part in the Programme?

Mentees

  • All 2026 Commonwealth Scholars studying in the UK
  • Continuing PhD Scholars

Mentors

  • All Commonwealth Alumni who have studied in the UK and have at least one year post-Scholarship
  • Current Mentors may apply to take part for another year

What Does It Mean If I Apply and Am Not Paired?

There are a greater number of eligible Commonwealth Alumni than incoming Scholars. This typically means the programme receives more applications for Mentors than Mentees and as such, not all Mentor applications can be paired.

Pairings are made based on application responses across a number of areas, including: pairing country preference; Mentor and Mentee subject and/or field of study; topic area; key words; motivations for becoming a Mentor/Mentee; and the professional experience of a Mentor.

Will I Receive Feedback on My Application?

We are unable to provide feedback on individual applications. We encourage all unsuccessful applicants to apply to the programme in future, or submit a request to volunteer for any similar opportunities by contacting the CSC Alumni Team at alumni@cscuk.org.uk.

About the CSC Mentoring Programme Pairing

Will I Have the Same Mentor/Mentee Throughout the Programme?

Yes, you will have the same Mentor/Mentee for the duration of the year-long cycle.

Will I Be Paired With a Mentor/Mentee From the Same Subject Area?

Pairings are based on a range of factors, including home-country or cross-country pairing preference, subject and/or field of study, topic area, key words, motivations for joining the programme, and the Mentor’s professional experience.

While subject area and field of study are considered, they are not the primary criteria for pairing. The CSC aims to create pairings that support meaningful knowledge-sharing, professional development, and mentoring relationships.

Where possible, applicants will be matched using the information provided in their applications. However, direct matches, where a Mentor and Mentee studied the same subject or attended the same institution, are uncommon and are not the primary aim of the programme.

Are All Pairings Successful?

During the programme, there is the possibility that not all pairings will continue for the full duration of the programme. In these situations, the Alumni Team will terminate the pairing. Reasons for unsuccessful pairings vary and some are outlined below:

  • Mentor/Mentee has not submitted their agreement form confirming participation
  • Mentor/Mentee is unable to continue due to personal, professional, or other unforeseen commitments
  • Mentor/Mentee mutually agree that the pairing is not suitable

The CSC cannot guarantee an alternative pairing if a mentoring pairing ends early. However, participants are encouraged to seek out alternative means of support through CSC activities.

What Should a Mentor/Mentee Do If There Is a Disagreement?

You should refer to the section on constructive feedback in Mentoring Programme Handbooks available on the CSC website. The information on constructive feedback will support pairs in having healthy and positive mentoring conversations.

If you still have any concerns about how to go about this or are unable to reconcile differences, please contact alumni@cscuk.org.uk.

Can a Mentor Engage a Third Person or Expert to Help Their Mentee Regarding a Specific Need?

The CSC Mentoring Programme is based on a one-to-one relationship between a Mentor and Mentee. However, where appropriate, a Mentor may recommend or facilitate contact with a third party who can provide specialist advice or expertise relevant to the Mentee’s needs.

Before introducing a third party, the Mentor must obtain the consent of both individuals and must not share any personal information, including names or contact details, without their prior agreement.

Can Mentors Proof-Read Essays?

Mentors can provide guidance, look at sections of work, but should not edit whole chapters or essays, as this is not the purpose of a Mentor.

If a Mentee Goes to the Same University as Their Mentor, and Is Doing a Similar Course, Can They Share Notes or Past Exams Papers?

This practice can be frowned upon in some UK institutions. Mentees should contact their course coordinator if they wish to view or access these materials.

Meeting Your Mentor/Mentee

Who Should Initiate the First Introduction?

The Mentor should make the first contact by email and introduce themselves to their Mentee. This initial introduction helps establish the mentoring relationship, set expectations, and begin planning future communication.

You can read guidance on the type of information to share in initial communications in the Mentoring Programme Handbooks.

Is a Physical Meeting Between Mentors and Mentees Allowed?

The CSC Mentoring Programme is designed primarily as a virtual programme, as Mentors and Mentees are often based in different countries during the Scholarship period.

If a Mentor and Mentee happen to be in the same location and both wish to meet in person, they may do so at their own discretion. Any in-person meeting should be arranged by mutual agreement, take place in a safe and appropriate setting, and comply with any relevant local guidance or regulations (for instance, COVID regulations).

Neither Mentor nor Mentee should feel obligated to meet in person, and either party may decline such a meeting if they are uncomfortable doing so.

What Is the Minimum Commitment to Meet Every Month?

The minimum commitment of engagement is two hours every month. You can organise this time in whatever way works best for your goals and time commitments.

Can I Meet With My Mentor/Mentee More Than 2 Hours in a Month?

Yes, you can. You will both need to agree meetings and time commitments.

What If I Do Not Hear From My Mentor/Mentee?

When contacting your Mentor/Mentee, keep in mind that they may have reasons to not respond immediately. The reasons could include important work/study deadlines, travel, illness, or other personal reasons. Always provide a sufficient deadline for them to respond by and if you still fail to hear back, notify the CSC Alumni Team at alumni@cscuk.org.uk.

CSC Mentoring Programme Goal Setting

What Type of Goals Can I Set?

It is important to set clear goals at the start of the cycle so you know what support your Mentor/Mentee needs to provide, and you understand what you can ask them about. Goals may relate to academic, professional, and personal growth. Please refer to the SMART goals framework in the Mentoring Programme Handbooks.

Should Mentors Set Goals?

Yes. The CSC Mentoring Programme is a two-way learning experience, and Mentors are encouraged to set goals for their own development, as well as support their Mentee in achieving theirs.

As a Mentor, consider what you hope to gain from the experience, the skills you would like to develop, and what you would like to learn from your Mentee.

Examples of Mentor goals include: developing mentorking, leadership and professional skills, building meaningful connections, expanding knowledge of a different sector, country, or professional context, building meaningful connections within the Commonwealth community.

Please refer to the SMART goals framework in the Mentoring Programme Handbooks.

After the CSC Mentoring Programme

Will I Get a Certificate for Participating in the Programme?

Participants who complete the full mentoring cycle and complete the final feedback survey will receive a certificate confirming their participation.

Can Mentors and Mentees Stay in Touch After the Programme?

We encourage Mentors and Mentees to discuss whether they would like to keep in contact following the end of the formal programme and you should discuss this during the final stage. It is important to remember that the dynamics of this relationship may be different post-programme.

Apply for the CSC Mentoring Programme 2026-27

The CSC Mentoring Programme 2026-27 provides Commonwealth Scholars and Alumni with an opportunity to build meaningful professional connections, exchange knowledge, strengthen mentoring and leadership skills, and support development impact.

The application deadline is 23:59 (BST) on Sunday 11 October 2026.

For further information, visit the CSC Mentoring Programme page and read the CSC Mentoring Programme – FAQs.

For questions about the programme or how to apply, contact alumni@cscuk.org.uk.

item.content:encoded:
The Brunel University of London and China Scholarship Council (CSC) PhD Scholarship 2027/28 offers academically outstanding Chinese students an opportunity to pursue a fully funded PhD at Brunel University of London in the United Kingdom.

For the 2027/28 intake, 20 full scholarships are available for PhD studies commencing in October 2027 or January 2028. The scholarships are jointly supported by Brunel University of London and the China Scholarship Council.

The funding package includes full tuition fees for up to 48 months, a living-cost stipend including medical insurance, one international round-trip economy-class airfare between China and the UK, and reimbursement of one-off visa application fees.

About the Brunel University and CSC PhD Scholarship

The scholarship programme is designed to provide academically strong Chinese students with the opportunity to undertake doctoral research at Brunel University of London.

The 2027/28 programme offers:

  • 20 full PhD scholarships
  • Study at Brunel University of London
  • Scholarships available across all disciplines
  • PhD programmes commencing in October 2027 or January 2028
  • Up to 48 months of tuition fee coverage
  • Living-cost stipend from CSC
  • Medical insurance
  • International return airfare between China and the UK
  • Reimbursement of one-off visa application fees

The available PhD programmes can be explored through Brunel University’s programme listings.

Scholarship Benefits

Full Tuition Fee Coverage

Brunel University of London will provide full tuition fee funding for up to 48 months for each successful scholarship recipient.

Living-Cost Stipend

The China Scholarship Council will provide a stipend to support living costs during the scholarship period.

The stipend also includes medical insurance.

International Airfare

Each scholarship recipient will receive funding for one international round-trip economy-class airfare between China and the UK.

Visa Application Fee

CSC will reimburse the successful recipient for one-off visa application fees.

PhD Study Duration

The scholarship can support PhD studies for up to 48 months.

Successful applicants are expected to commence their doctoral studies in either:

  • October 2027, or
  • January 2028

Available Fields of Study

The scholarships are available for PhD studies across all disciplines at Brunel University of London.

Applicants should explore Brunel’s available research degree programmes and identify a PhD programme that matches their academic background and proposed research interests.

Who Can Apply?

The Brunel University and CSC PhD Scholarship is specifically intended for eligible Chinese students.

Applicants must meet the following requirements:

  • Be a citizen of the People’s Republic of China.
  • Overseas Chinese students may be eligible depending on CSC policy applicable at the time of application.
  • Have a strong academic background.
  • Meet Brunel University’s academic entry requirements.
  • Meet Brunel University’s English language entry requirements.
  • Meet the relevant requirements of the China Scholarship Council.
  • Obtain the necessary UK visa to enter and study in the UK.

Applicants should also carefully review the CSC’s own eligibility criteria because meeting Brunel University’s requirements alone does not guarantee eligibility for CSC funding.

Current Brunel PhD Students

Current first-year PhD students at Brunel University of London may also be eligible under specific conditions.

Students who started their PhD after January 2026 can apply and will be considered by CSC in open competition alongside other applicants.

If successful, their CSC scholarship funding will begin from the second year of their PhD.

Current first-year PhD students have additional application requirements, including a short personal statement of no more than 750 words explaining their research topic and supervisor, as well as a recommendation letter from their supervisor confirming that they have successfully passed the nine-month progress review.

These materials must be submitted before the deadline to:

internationalsponsorship@brunel.ac.uk

Application Deadline

The deadline for the Brunel University of London application is:

8 January 2027 at 12:00 AM

Applicants are strongly encouraged to apply early rather than waiting until the deadline.

How to Apply

The application process involves two main stages: first applying to Brunel University of London and then, if nominated, applying to the China Scholarship Council.

Step 1: Identify a Suitable Supervisor

Applicants should contact the relevant Brunel University department or academic staff member to identify a suitable PhD supervisor.

Potential supervisors and their research expertise can be explored through Brunel University’s staff directory.

Applicants should establish that their proposed research aligns with the expertise of the prospective supervisor.

Step 2: Apply for PhD Admission to Brunel

Applicants must apply online for admission to a Brunel PhD programme before 8 January 2027.

Brunel University assesses applications received by the deadline before selecting candidates for nomination to CSC.

Early application is strongly recommended.

Step 3: Select the Correct Funding Option

When completing the Brunel online application, applicants must indicate that they intend to apply for the:

BUL/CSC Joint Scholarship Scheme

In the Fees and Funding section of the application, applicants should:

  1. Select Funded.
  2. Select China Scholarship Council (CSC) as the funding option.
  3. Include the name of their potential supervisor.

This is an important part of the application process.

Step 4: Brunel Reviews Applications

Brunel University will assess applications submitted by the January deadline.

The university expects to select applicants for nomination to CSC by the end of February 2027.

Successful nominees will receive a Brunel offer letter.

Step 5: Apply to CSC

After being nominated by Brunel, successful applicants must apply directly to the China Scholarship Council during its application window.

The CSC application period is expected to take place in March 2027.

Applicants should check the official CSC website for the confirmed application dates and requirements.

Step 6: CSC Selection

Brunel expects to receive the final list of successful CSC scholarship recipients in late May or early June 2027.

Successful applicants will then proceed toward their PhD studies at Brunel.

Application Timeline

Stage Expected Date
Brunel application deadline 8 January 2027
Brunel selects CSC nominees End of February 2027
CSC application period Expected March 2027
CSC results received by Brunel Late May/Early June 2027
PhD commencement October 2027 or January 2028

Application Documents and Preparation

Applicants should prepare their PhD application carefully and ensure that their proposed research is appropriate for their selected programme and prospective supervisor.

Depending on the applicant’s circumstances, preparation may include:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Evidence of English language proficiency
  • Research proposal and related application materials
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Details of proposed research
  • Potential supervisor information
  • Brunel PhD application
  • CSC scholarship application

Applicants should follow Brunel University’s specific research degree application requirements and the CSC’s requirements separately.

Important Information for Current Brunel PhD Students

Current first-year Brunel PhD students who started after January 2026 have a separate requirement.

They must submit:

  • A personal statement of no more than 750 words
  • A description of their research subject
  • The name of their supervisor
  • A recommendation letter from their supervisor
  • Confirmation that they successfully passed the nine-month progress review

These materials should be sent to:

internationalsponsorship@brunel.ac.uk

before the application deadline.

Why Apply for This Scholarship?

The Brunel University and CSC partnership provides successful candidates with substantial financial support for doctoral study in the UK.

The combined funding package covers major study-related costs, including:

  • Tuition fees
  • Living expenses
  • Medical insurance
  • International travel
  • One-off visa application fees

The scholarship also provides an opportunity to undertake doctoral research at Brunel University of London across a wide range of disciplines.

Important Considerations

Admission Comes Before the CSC Application

Applicants must first apply to Brunel and receive an offer before applying to CSC.

Therefore, prospective applicants should begin the Brunel admission process well ahead of the January deadline.

Scholarship Selection Is Separate

Receiving a Brunel offer does not automatically mean that an applicant will receive CSC funding.

Brunel first selects applicants for nomination, after which nominated candidates submit their applications directly to CSC.

Check Both Sets of Requirements

Applicants must satisfy both:

  • Brunel University’s PhD admission requirements, and
  • China Scholarship Council eligibility requirements.

Start Early

Because applicants need to identify a supervisor, prepare a PhD application and subsequently apply to CSC if nominated, early preparation is strongly recommended.

Conclusion

The Brunel University of London and China Scholarship Council PhD Scholarship 2027/28 provides 20 fully funded PhD opportunities for eligible Chinese students seeking doctoral study in the United Kingdom.

Successful candidates can receive full tuition fee coverage for up to 48 months, a CSC living-cost stipend including medical insurance, an international round-trip economy-class flight between China and the UK, and reimbursement of one-off visa application fees.

The scholarship is open across Brunel’s PhD disciplines, with studies expected to begin in October 2027 or January 2028.

Applicants must first apply to Brunel University and obtain an offer before proceeding to the CSC application stage. The Brunel application deadline is 8 January 2027, so prospective applicants should begin identifying suitable supervisors and preparing their applications early.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The M Health Fairview Center for Community Health Equity is advancing community health equity through partnerships, research, leadership development and initiatives focused on addressing the social and structural factors that influence health outcomes.

As part of this work, M Health Fairview has announced the Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship, a year-long leadership development programme designed to support community leaders working on innovative projects that promote health equity and address the social determinants of health.

The Center works alongside community partners toward a shared goal of improving the health of the communities it serves. It is located within the Fairview Community Health and Wellness Hub and provides a space for M Health Fairview and community partners to collaborate on reducing racial and other disparities in community health outcomes.

About the M Health Fairview Center for Community Health Equity

The Center for Community Health Equity extends the work of M Health Fairview’s Community Advancement team.

Its approach brings together the health system, community organizations, leaders and residents to address factors that influence health beyond traditional clinical care.

The Center’s work is built around three key strategies:

1. Community Incubator

This strategy focuses on addressing the social determinants and drivers of health as well as individual social risk factors.

2. Engagement Infrastructure

The Center works to build trusting partnerships while creating opportunities for community and patient voices to inform its work.

3. Inclusive Institution

The Center also works toward transforming structures to create an increasingly equitable and inclusive environment.

Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship

The newly launched Accelerator Fellowship is a year-long leadership development programme.

The fellowship is designed to support community leaders who are advancing innovative projects focused on:

  • Health equity
  • Social determinants of health
  • Community improvement
  • Innovative community-based solutions

 

The available source introduces the fellowship but does not provide detailed information about the application deadline, number of fellows, funding amount, eligibility requirements or application procedure.

Therefore, applicants should consult the official M Health Fairview information before making assumptions about these details.

Understanding the Social Determinants of Health

M Health Fairview states that research shows 80% of health occurs outside hospitals and clinics. The organization therefore emphasizes the importance of addressing social determinants of health through enhanced models of care and service delivery.

This approach recognizes that factors outside traditional healthcare settings can influence the health and wellbeing of communities.

The Center’s initiatives address several of these broader factors.

Key Social Determinants of Health Initiatives

Food Is Medicine

The Food is Medicine initiative focuses on using food to support patients, strengthen communities and contribute to system-level change.

The initiative reflects the Center’s focus on improving access to resources that contribute to community health.

Housing Is Health

The Housing is Health initiative focuses on stable and affordable housing as an important foundation for strong communities and inclusive growth.

Connection Is Cure

The Connection is Cure initiative focuses on building trust through social connections, recognizing linguistic and cultural diversity and connecting communities with the health system.

Population Health Equity Initiatives

M Health Fairview also applies equity-centered and culturally responsive approaches to healthcare.

According to the Center, its approach involves:

  1. Identifying challenges and opportunities.
  2. Creating or expanding programmes and partnerships.
  3. Testing and developing solutions.
  4. Scaling or deepening successful approaches across the health system and communities.

 

Current population health equity initiatives include the Native Health Equity Initiative and Birth Justice Initiative.

Native Health Equity Initiative

The initiative, known as Healing in Four Directions, seeks to build trust and establish partnerships to better serve Native patients, employees and community members.

Birth Justice Initiative

The Birth Justice Initiative is a cross-departmental effort involving community members, patients, providers and employees.

It focuses on aligning and amplifying equity-driven solutions to improve outcomes for birthing individuals and their babies.

Who Is the Accelerator Fellowship For?

The information provided by M Health Fairview describes the Accelerator Fellowship as a programme for community leaders who are advancing innovative projects related to health equity and social determinants of health.

However, the available source does not specify:

  • A minimum or maximum age
  • Citizenship requirements
  • Academic requirements
  • Geographic eligibility
  • Professional experience requirements
  • Number of fellows selected
  • Whether the programme provides a stipend or grant
  • Application deadline
  • Application form or submission procedure

Prospective applicants should therefore check the official fellowship information for the latest application details.

Why the Fellowship Matters

Community health challenges often extend beyond healthcare facilities.

The Accelerator Fellowship’s focus on leadership development and innovative community projects connects directly with the Center’s broader approach of working with community partners to improve health outcomes.

The programme may therefore be relevant to community leaders developing solutions that address issues affecting health and wellbeing at the community level.

M Health Fairview’s Community-Based Approach

The Center builds on M Health Fairview’s existing partnerships with:

  • Government organizations
  • Community-based nonprofits
  • Private organizations
  • Community leaders
  • Patients and residents

The organization describes this as part of a long-standing commitment to addressing the social determinants of health.

This partnership-based approach is central to the Center’s efforts to develop and expand health equity initiatives.

Center for Community Health Equity Workgroup

The Center’s work is supported by a workgroup made up of experts from across the M Health Fairview health system.

The workgroup provides leadership and helps shape and guide the Center’s work.

Members include professionals from areas such as:

  • Family medicine
  • Health equity research
  • Health disparities research
  • Pediatrics
  • Behavioral neuroscience
  • Health informatics
  • Quality improvement
  • Community engagement
  • Inclusive excellence

How to Learn More

Individuals interested in the Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship should review the official M Health Fairview information for application details as they become available.

The Center’s official page provides additional information about its work and the Accelerator Fellowship.

Official information:
https://www.mhealthfairview.org/about-us/health-equity/m-health-fairview-center-for-community-health-equity/cche

Conclusion

The M Health Fairview Center for Community Health Equity brings together healthcare professionals, community partners and other stakeholders to address health disparities and the social factors that influence community health.

Its newly launched Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship provides a year-long leadership development opportunity for community leaders working on innovative projects that promote health equity and address social determinants of health.

Beyond the fellowship, the Center’s wider work includes initiatives focused on food access, housing, social connection, Native health equity and birth justice.

Prospective applicants should monitor the official M Health Fairview page for detailed fellowship eligibility, funding, application requirements and deadlines when those details are published.

Discover more fellowship opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) is currently inviting applications for several opportunities across its professional, general services, short-term, consultancy and internship categories.

These openings provide opportunities for professionals and early-career applicants interested in contributing to international climate action through the UNFCCC Secretariat.

The current openings include positions in technology, mitigation, adaptation, communications and engagement, markets and non-market support, as well as other areas connected to the UNFCCC’s work.

Current UNFCCC Vacancies

The current vacancies are divided into four main categories: fixed-term employment, short-term employment, consultancy and internship opportunities.

1. Fixed-Term Employment Opportunities

Programme Officer — P-3

Programme: Technology Subdivision, Means of Implementation (MOI) Division

Level: P-3

Application Period: 11 September – 27 September 2026

Announcement Number: VA 26/041/MoI

The Programme Officer position is part of the Technology Subdivision within the Means of Implementation Division.

Interested applicants should review the official vacancy announcement for the detailed responsibilities, qualifications and application requirements.

Programme Assistant — G-5

Programme: Constituted Bodies and Data Services Subdivision, Mitigation Division

Level: G-5

Application Period: 18 September – 4 October 2026

Announcement Number: VA 26/042/M

This is a General Services position within the Mitigation Division.

Applicants should consult the official vacancy announcement for complete information about the role and required qualifications.

2. Short-Term Employment

Associate Programme Officer — P-2

Programme: Vulnerability Subdivision, Adaptation Division

Level: P-2

Application Period: 18 September – 4 October 2026

Announcement Number: 26/TJO13/A

The position is located within the Adaptation Division’s Vulnerability Subdivision.

The detailed vacancy announcement should be reviewed carefully before applying.

3. Consultancy Opportunity

Consultant — Technical Paper on Enhancing Observer Engagement

Programme: Communications & Engagement Division

Level: N/A

Application Period: 18 September – 4 October 2026

Announcement Number: 26/CON10/C&E

The consultancy supports work on a technical paper on enhancing observer engagement under SBI Arrangements for Intergovernmental Meetings.

Applicants should consult the official announcement for the complete consultancy scope, deliverables, qualifications and submission requirements.

4. Internship Opportunity

Intern — Mitigation, Markets and Non-Market Support

Programme: Mitigation, Markets and non-markets support

Level: N/A

Application Period: 24 September – 18 October 2026

Announcement Number: 25/Intern29/M-Market and non-markets support

This internship provides an opportunity for an early-career applicant to gain experience within the UNFCCC’s work on mitigation, markets and non-market approaches.

Applicants should review the official internship vacancy announcement for the complete requirements.

UNFCCC Application Deadlines

Applicants should pay close attention to the individual closing dates because each vacancy has a different application period.

Position Category Level Deadline
Programme Officer Fixed-term P-3 27 September 2026
Programme Assistant Fixed-term G-5 4 October 2026
Associate Programme Officer Short-term P-2 4 October 2026
Consultant Consultancy N/A 4 October 2026
Intern Internship N/A 18 October 2026

How to Apply for UNFCCC Vacancies

The UNFCCC states that applicants should only use its online application system when applying for vacancy announcements.

Step 1: Register

Click the Apply Now button associated with the vacancy you are interested in.

Applicants will first be asked to register as users with the UNFCCC Online Application System.

Step 2: Complete the Application

After registration, applicants can apply for a vacancy by completing their Personal History Form (P.11) through the online system.

Applicants can also save their profile so that information can be updated and used for future vacancy applications.

Step 3: Submit the Application

Applicants should carefully review their information before submitting the completed online application.

The UNFCCC advises applicants not to attach additional documents during the initial online application process.

If an applicant is invited for an interview, they may subsequently be required to provide documentary evidence supporting information included in the application.

Step 4: Check the Acknowledgement Email

After submitting an online application, applicants should receive an acknowledgement by email.

The UNFCCC states that if an acknowledgement is not received within 24 hours, applicants should contact:

vacancies@unfccc.int

Applicants who receive the automatic notification do not need to submit another application through another method.

Application Preparation Tips

Review the Specific Vacancy Announcement

Each position has its own announcement and requirements. Applicants should read the relevant vacancy announcement carefully before applying.

Prepare Your Personal History Form

The UNFCCC uses the P.11 Personal History Form as part of its online application process. Applicants should ensure that their information is accurate and complete.

Apply Before the Closing Time

Do not wait until the final hours to submit an application. Allow sufficient time for registration, completing the application and receiving the submission acknowledgement.

Check Your Email

After submitting an application, monitor the email address associated with your UNFCCC application account for the acknowledgement and any subsequent communication.

Opportunities Across Climate Action

The current UNFCCC openings cover several areas connected to international climate policy and implementation.

The vacancies span:

  • Technology
  • Means of implementation
  • Mitigation
  • Adaptation
  • Vulnerability
  • Communications and engagement
  • Observer engagement
  • Climate markets
  • Non-market approaches

This range demonstrates the variety of professional functions involved in supporting the UNFCCC’s work.

Conclusion

The UNFCCC Current Openings 2026 provide several opportunities for professionals, early-career applicants and specialists interested in contributing to international climate action.

The available positions include Programme Officer, Programme Assistant, Associate Programme Officer, Consultant and Intern opportunities across different UNFCCC divisions.

Applicants should carefully review the individual vacancy announcements, confirm that they meet the relevant requirements and submit their applications through the official UNFCCC online application system before the applicable deadline.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The Center for Eastern European Studies (CEES) at the University of Zurich is inviting applications for its Spring 2027 Fellowship Program, offering 5–6 residential fellowships to highly talented and innovative young or mid-career scholars in the social sciences and humanities.

The fellowship provides an opportunity to spend up to four months in Zurich, pursue independent research, participate in the academic activities of CEES, and engage with an interdisciplinary community of scholars working on Russia, Eastern Europe, the Caucasus and Central Asia.

About the CEES Fellowship Program

The CEES Fellowship is normally structured as a four-month residential fellowship during one academic semester.

For the Spring 2027 semester, the fellowship will begin in mid-February 2027.

The programme welcomes research proposals addressing historical or contemporary topics related to:

  • Russia
  • Eastern Europe
  • The Caucasus
  • Central Asia
  • Post-Soviet Eurasia

For the Spring 2027 fellowship cycle, CEES is particularly interested in scholars researching:

  • Geopolitical trends
  • Economic connectivity
  • Transnational social issues
  • Transnational cultural issues
  • The South Caucasus region

Fellowship Duration

The fellowship will last for up to four months, beginning in mid-February 2027.

During their residency, fellows are expected to focus on their independent research while actively participating in the scholarly activities of the Center for Eastern European Studies.

What Does the Fellowship Provide?

The CEES Fellowship provides several forms of support to selected scholars.

Living Expenses

The fellowship includes a stipend for living expenses during the fellowship period of up to four months.

Travel and Administrative Costs

Funding also covers travel and administrative costs in Switzerland.

Workspace and Facilities

Fellows receive access to:

  • A workspace at CEES
  • Relevant libraries
  • Necessary research facilities
  • The interdisciplinary academic community associated with CEES

Housing Support

CEES will assist fellows with finding housing in the Zurich area during their residency.

Research and Academic Activities

The fellowship is not solely a research stay. Fellows are expected to actively participate in the academic environment at CEES.

During the fellowship, selected scholars will:

  • Pursue independent research in residence.
  • Participate actively in CEES scholarly activities.
  • Access relevant libraries and research resources.
  • Present their research topic in a workshop.
  • Engage with the interdisciplinary community of experts associated with CEES.
  • Publish their findings through one of the CEES publication outlets.

Who Can Apply?

The fellowship is intended for young or mid-career scholars working in the:

  • Social sciences
  • Humanities

Applicants should have a research focus addressing historical or contemporary topics connected to Russia, Eastern Europe, the Caucasus or Central Asia.

For Spring 2027, applications connected to the South Caucasus and focusing on geopolitical trends, economic connectivity, or transnational social and cultural issues are particularly welcomed.

Important Eligibility Requirement

Applicants must be enrolled or employed at their home university.

This means the fellowship is intended for scholars who maintain an academic affiliation with their home institution during the application and fellowship process.

Application Requirements

A complete application must contain all of the following materials:

1. Letter of Motivation

Applicants should submit a letter explaining their motivation for applying to the CEES Fellowship Program.

2. Research Proposal

A 3–5 page research proposal is required.

The proposal should clearly present the research project the applicant intends to pursue during the fellowship.

3. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must provide a CV that includes a list of publications.

4. Writing Sample

Applicants should provide a short writing sample, such as an:

  • Academic article
  • Book chapter

5. CEES Presentation Proposal

Applicants must also submit a short proposal for the presentation they would give at CEES during their fellowship.

6. References

Applicants must provide two letters of recommendation and/or the names of two referees.

Language and Submission Format

All application materials must be written in English.

The complete application should be combined into one single PDF document.

Applications should be sent by email to:

cees@isos.uzh.ch

Application Deadline

The deadline for the Spring 2027 CEES Fellowship is:

12 October 2026

Applicants should ensure that the complete application reaches CEES by the stated deadline.

Fellowship Timeline

Detail Information
Fellowship CEES Fellowship Program
Semester Spring 2027
Location University of Zurich, Switzerland
Number of Fellowships 5–6
Duration Up to 4 months
Start Mid-February 2027
Target Applicants Young and mid-career scholars
Fields Social sciences and humanities
Application Language English
Deadline 12 October 2026
Application Format Single PDF
Email cees@isos.uzh.ch

Areas of Research Interest

CEES welcomes research proposals across topics related to Eastern Europe and post-Soviet Eurasia.

For this particular fellowship cycle, applicants with research interests in the South Caucasus are especially encouraged to consider the programme where their work addresses areas such as:

  • Geopolitical developments
  • Economic connectivity
  • Cross-border social dynamics
  • Transnational cultural issues

Research may focus on historical or contemporary issues within the broader geographic scope of the fellowship.

How to Apply

Interested scholars should prepare all required application materials in English and combine them into a single PDF document.

The application should contain:

  1. Letter of motivation
  2. 3–5 page research proposal
  3. CV with publication list
  4. Short writing sample
  5. Proposal for the CEES presentation
  6. Two recommendation letters and/or names of two referees

The completed PDF should then be emailed to:

cees@isos.uzh.ch

Application Preparation Tips

Applicants should ensure that their research proposal clearly demonstrates what they intend to accomplish during the four-month residency.

It is also important to ensure that the writing sample, CV and presentation proposal complement the research project described in the application.

Because the fellowship requires active participation in CEES activities, applicants should also demonstrate how their research can contribute to the Center’s interdisciplinary academic environment.

Funding

The CEES Fellowship provides financial support covering:

  • Living expenses through a stipend
  • Travel costs in Switzerland
  • Administrative costs in Switzerland

Selected fellows also receive research facilities, workspace and library access.

CEES will assist fellows in finding accommodation in the Zurich area.

About CEES

The Center for Eastern European Studies (CEES) is based at the University of Zurich and supports interdisciplinary research and scholarly exchange focused on Eastern Europe and post-Soviet Eurasia.

The CEES Fellowship Program is funded by the Department of History and supported by the University of Zurich.

Conclusion

The CEES Fellowship Program 2027 provides young and mid-career scholars in the social sciences and humanities with an opportunity to undertake independent research in residence at the University of Zurich.

The programme offers 5–6 residential fellowships lasting up to four months, with financial support for living expenses, travel and administrative costs, as well as access to research facilities and an interdisciplinary scholarly network.

Applicants working on Russia, Eastern Europe, the Caucasus or Central Asia are eligible to consider the programme, with particular interest for the Spring 2027 cycle in research addressing the South Caucasus, geopolitical trends, economic connectivity and transnational social or cultural issues.

The application deadline is 12 October 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The NFL Rotational Program 2027 offers current undergraduate seniors an opportunity to begin a full-time career with the National Football League through a highly selective, two-year rotational programme.

Participants can complete up to four project-based rotations across different NFL offices and departments, gaining experience in areas such as communications, finance, football operations, marketing, broadcasting, international business, events, media and more.

The programme offers a listed salary of $72,000 USD and is scheduled to begin in July 2027.

About the NFL Rotational Program

The NFL Rotational Program is designed to give participants broad professional experience through challenging assignments, League events and networking opportunities across different areas of the organization.

During the two-year programme, participants may complete up to four rotations depending on business needs, their performance and previous experience.

Potential locations include:

  • NFL League Office — New York
  • NFL Media — California
  • NFL Government Affairs Office — Washington, DC
  • NFL Films — New Jersey

The specific department assigned during each rotation will be determined according to the NFL’s business needs.

Departments and Areas of Work

Previous programme rotations have included a wide range of business functions, including:

  • Communications & Public Affairs
  • Events Strategy
  • Finance
  • Football Operations
  • International
  • Marketing & Sales
  • Broadcasting
  • Labor Operations
  • Media

The programme can therefore provide exposure to different aspects of professional sports operations and business.

Who Can Apply?

The NFL is considering applications from currently enrolled undergraduate seniors, including students completing a fifth consecutive year.

Applicants must:

  • Be graduating between Winter 2026 and Spring 2027.
  • Have an overall GPA of 3.0 or above.
  • Be available to begin the two-year programme in July 2027.
  • Be legally permitted to work in the United States.
  • Have all required visas and U.S. employment authorizations before the programme begins if they are international students.
  • Be willing to relocate to any NFL League office for a rotation during the two-year programme.
  • Have strong internship or previous work experience.
  • Demonstrate an interest in gaining diverse professional experience within professional sports.

Required Skills and Qualifications

Applicants are expected to demonstrate strong professional and interpersonal capabilities.

The NFL lists the following qualifications and skills:

Microsoft Office

Applicants should have advanced experience using:

  • Microsoft Word
  • Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Microsoft Excel

Communication and Relationship Management

Candidates should demonstrate:

  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Strong communication skills
  • Relationship management abilities
  • Excellent presentation skills

Analytical and Organizational Skills

Applicants should also demonstrate:

  • Independent thinking
  • Strong attention to detail
  • Analytical and critical-thinking skills
  • Planning and organizational abilities
  • Strong time-management skills

Adaptability and Collaboration

Participants are expected to be able to adapt to different work environments, leadership styles and teams.

The ability to work collaboratively across functions is also required.

Programme Responsibilities

Participants will undertake project-based assignments during each rotation.

The work may involve different departments depending on the NFL’s current organizational needs and the participant’s previous experience and performance.

The rotational structure is intended to provide exposure to different professional functions rather than placing participants permanently in one department from the beginning.

Two-Year Programme Structure

The programme is a full-time two-year rotational opportunity.

Participants may complete up to four rotations during this period.

At the end of the programme, participants may choose to pursue:

  • Internal opportunities within the NFL
  • Further education
  • Opportunities with NFL Clubs
  • Opportunities with partner organizations
  • Career opportunities outside the NFL

Continued employment with the NFL after the scheduled end of the rotational programme is not guaranteed.

Work Location and Relocation

The programme requires participants to be available for onsite work.

Potential rotation locations include New York, California, Washington, DC and New Jersey.

Participants must therefore be willing to relocate to an NFL League office when required by their rotation placement.

No relocation assistance will be provided.

The position does not offer remote or hybrid working options. The NFL states that in-person work at its offices is a priority for collaboration, professional connections and organizational culture.

Working Hours

NFL employees are expected to work 40 hours per week.

Occasional travel may also be required depending on the participant’s rotation placement.

Salary

The advertised salary for the NFL Rotational Program is:

$72,000 USD

The posting indicates that the NFL expects to hire near the middle of the stated salary range. The listed salary amount is $72,000.

Applicants should also review the NFL’s official benefits information for details of its employee benefits package.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

Wednesday, September 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET

Only fully completed eligible applications will be considered.

Applicants should ensure that they submit an updated resume as part of their application.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should apply through the NFL’s official employer application portal.

Before submitting an application, candidates should ensure that they:

  1. Meet the graduation requirements.
  2. Have a minimum GPA of 3.0.
  3. Confirm their U.S. work authorization.
  4. Prepare an updated resume.
  5. Review their previous internship and work experience.
  6. Confirm their availability to begin in July 2027.
  7. Be prepared to relocate for different rotations.
  8. Submit the completed application before the deadline.

Official Application: NFL Careers – Rotational Program

What the NFL Looks For

Beyond the formal qualifications, the NFL describes several attributes expected of employees.

These include:

  • An enthusiastic and proactive attitude
  • Willingness to learn
  • Strong work ethic
  • Adaptability
  • Relationship-building skills
  • Ability to influence and collaborate
  • Resilience and persistence
  • Passion for professional growth

The NFL also identifies leadership attributes such as building talent, executing effectively, inspiring others, living organizational values, understanding the business and thinking ambitiously.

Important Considerations for Applicants

1. Confirm Your Graduation Date

The programme is specifically aimed at students graduating between Winter 2026 and Spring 2027.

2. Check Your Work Authorization

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. International students must have the necessary visas and U.S. employment authorizations before the programme begins.

3. Prepare an Updated Resume

The NFL specifically states that only fully completed eligible applications will be considered and requires an updated resume.

4. Be Prepared to Relocate

Rotation placement can require relocation to different NFL offices, so applicants should consider this requirement before applying.

5. Apply Before the Deadline

Applications close at 11:59 PM ET on September 30, 2026.

Conclusion

The NFL Rotational Program 2027 provides graduating undergraduate students with a structured opportunity to gain professional experience across multiple areas of the National Football League.

The two-year programme can include up to four rotations across NFL offices and departments, with project-based assignments, networking opportunities and exposure to different areas of professional sports operations.

Eligible students graduating between Winter 2026 and Spring 2027 with a GPA of at least 3.0 should review the requirements carefully and submit a complete application before the September 30, 2026 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
Deadline: October 13, 2026

IREX is seeking academic, professional, and regional experts to serve as application readers for the 2027 Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders.

About the Mandela Washington Fellowship

The Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders is the flagship exchange program of the Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI).

In summer 2027, the Fellowship will bring up to 550 accomplished young African leaders to the United States for a comprehensive, executive-style program designed to strengthen leadership skills, build professional networks, and support collaboration between African and American counterparts.

Fellows participate in academic coursework, professional site visits, and structured networking activities. The program focuses on strengthening collaboration in areas including U.S.-Africa trade and economic prosperity, technological innovation, and peace and security.

The Mandela Washington Fellowship is a program of the U.S. Department of State, funded by the U.S. Government and administered by IREX.

Call for Application Readers

IREX is looking for individuals who can review and score applications using established guidelines and a structured scoring rubric.

Over the past twelve years, application readers have helped assess nearly 478,000 applications from 49 sub-Saharan African countries for approximately 7,800 Fellowship places.

Serving as an application reader provides an opportunity to contribute to a fair and merit-based selection process while gaining insight into emerging priorities, challenges, and locally driven solutions across Sub-Saharan Africa.

Readers may also gain valuable exposure to fellowship selection practices, promising African leaders, and key issues affecting the continent.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is particularly suited to academics, professionals, and regional experts with expertise in one or more of the Fellowship’s thematic areas:

  • Business and trade
  • Emerging technologies
  • Governance and security

Experience working in Africa or on sub-Saharan African issues is also relevant.

While expertise in these areas is ideal, it is not a requirement to serve as a reader.

Reader Honorarium

Eligible readers may opt to receive a one-time $100 honorarium for their service.

However:

  • U.S. Government employees and contractors are not eligible to receive the honorarium.
  • IREX cannot make international wire payments.
  • Readers receiving the honorarium must have a U.S. bank account in their own name capable of receiving an ACH/direct deposit transfer.
  • Eligible readers who choose to receive the honorarium must submit a completed W-9 form to IREX for tax purposes.

Application Deadline and Reading Period

Interested individuals should complete the 2027 Reader Application by:

📅 October 13, 2026

The application reading period is expected to begin in mid-October 2026 and continue through mid-November 2026. Selected readers will be contacted by IREX in October.

How to Apply

item.content:encoded:
BRAC, one of the world’s leading development organisations, is inviting applications for several Regular Internship opportunities in 2026 across different departments and programmes. These internships provide students, recent graduates and other qualified candidates with an opportunity to gain practical professional experience while contributing to the work of a globally recognised development organisation.

The current BRAC internship openings cover areas including Human Resources, executive support, microfinance, climate action, technology, finance and accounts. The internships are particularly relevant for candidates who want to build careers in international development, nonprofit management, finance, technology, human resources, climate and sustainability, operations, and related fields.

What Is the BRAC Regular Internship Programme?

The BRAC Regular Internship programme provides opportunities for individuals to gain hands-on experience within different functions of BRAC and its affiliated programmes and organisations.

BRAC operates across a broad range of development areas, and its internship opportunities can expose participants to real-world organisational, financial, technological, social-impact and development-related work.

Rather than simply providing classroom-based learning, an internship with BRAC can allow participants to understand how a large development organisation operates and how different departments contribute to its overall mission.

Depending on the specific internship, participants may work alongside professionals in areas such as:

  • Human resources and talent acquisition
  • Executive and organisational support
  • Microfinance
  • Operations and strategy
  • Climate and environmental programmes
  • Information technology
  • Finance and accounting
  • Treasury operations
  • Development and social-impact programmes

The exact responsibilities, qualifications, duration, location and other conditions vary according to the individual internship position.

Current BRAC Internship Opportunities

  1. Communications – Audiovisual Unit
    Application deadline: 26 September, 2026
  2. Communications – Campaign and Content Unit
    Application deadline: 26 September, 2026
  3. Migration Programme – Improved Sustainable Reintegration of Bangladeshi Returnee Migrants (Prottasha II)
    Application deadline: 26 September, 2026
  4. Otithi – Research and Operations
    Application deadline: 26 September, 2026
  5. Sir Fazle Hasan Abed Knowledge Hub – Research and project management
    Application deadline: 26 September, 2026
  6. Water, Sanitation and Hygiene – Equitable & Sustainable WASH Services in Bangladesh Delta Plan Hotspots (Technical Stream)
    Application deadline: 26 September, 2026
  7. Water, Sanitation and Hygiene – Equitable & Sustainable WASH Services in Bangladesh Delta Plan Hotspots (Community Stream)
    Application deadline: 26 September, 2026
  8. Social Compliance Programme
    Application deadline: 30 September, 2026
  9. Safeguarding and Grievance Management Department – Admin Unit
    Application deadline: 30 September, 2026
  10. BRAC Estate – Legal
    Application deadline: 17 October, 2026

Why Consider a BRAC Internship?

An internship with BRAC can provide more than an entry on a résumé. It can offer practical exposure to the operations of a major development organisation and help participants connect academic knowledge with real workplace responsibilities.

Some potential benefits include:

1. Practical Professional Experience

Interns can gain experience working within an established organisation and learn how professional teams manage projects, programmes and institutional responsibilities.

2. Exposure to International Development

BRAC is widely recognised for its work in development and social impact. Internships within its different programmes can help candidates understand how development initiatives are designed and implemented.

3. Career Development

Practical internship experience can strengthen a candidate’s résumé and demonstrate exposure to a professional working environment.

4. Department-Specific Experience

Because the current openings span multiple functions, candidates can pursue opportunities aligned with their academic background and career interests.

5. Understanding Organisational Operations

Interns can gain insight into how different teams, departments and programmes contribute to the functioning of a large organisation.

6. Opportunity to Apply Academic Knowledge

An internship can allow students and recent graduates to apply concepts learned through their academic programmes to practical workplace situations.

Who Can Apply for the BRAC Internships?

Eligibility varies according to the specific internship position. Applicants should therefore read the individual internship description carefully before applying.

The current opportunities are aimed at candidates whose academic background, skills and interests align with the relevant department.

Depending on the position, potentially relevant academic and professional backgrounds may include:

  • Business administration
  • Management
  • Finance
  • Accounting
  • Economics
  • Human resources
  • International development
  • Development studies
  • Environmental studies
  • Climate studies
  • Computer science
  • Information technology
  • Information systems
  • Public administration
  • Strategy and operations
  • Related disciplines

Applicants should not assume that studying one of these fields automatically makes them eligible. The precise academic qualifications, skills, experience and other requirements should be confirmed from the official description of each internship.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should follow these steps:

Step 1: Identify the Right Internship

Review the seven currently open positions and determine which one best matches your academic background, skills and career goals.

Step 2: Read the Full Internship Description

Click the relevant official BRAC internship description and carefully review the responsibilities and eligibility requirements.

Step 3: Prepare Your Application

Prepare the documents and information requested by BRAC for the particular internship.

Ensure that your résumé or CV highlights experiences that are relevant to the position.

Step 4: Check the Deadline

Because the positions have different closing dates, applicants should pay attention to the deadline for the specific position they are applying for.

Step 5: Submit Through the Official Channel

Follow the application instructions provided by BRAC for the selected internship.

Applicants should avoid relying on third-party websites for final application instructions when the official BRAC posting is available.

Click HERE to learn more and apply for the BRAC Regular Internships 2026.

Application Tips for Prospective BRAC Interns

Applicants can improve their preparation by following several practical steps.

Match Your Application to the Position

Do not use exactly the same résumé or application approach for every internship. Emphasise the experiences and skills most relevant to the specific department.

Highlight Practical Skills

If applying for an HR position, for example, highlight recruitment, administration, communication or people-management experience. For a technology position, emphasise relevant technical skills and projects.

Demonstrate Relevant Academic Knowledge

Connect your academic background to the responsibilities of the internship where appropriate.

Apply Before the Deadline

Do not wait until the final hours.

Verify the Official Requirements

The general internship page does not replace the individual job description. Always check the official PDF for the position you intend to apply for.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this a single BRAC internship?

No. The current BRAC Regular Internship page lists several separate internship opportunities across different departments and programmes.

Are the internships open to everyone?

No. Eligibility varies according to the individual internship. Applicants must meet the requirements specified for the position they wish to apply for.

Can students apply?

Potentially, depending on the requirements of the individual internship. Candidates should review the specific internship description for academic and other eligibility requirements.

Can graduates apply?

Potentially, depending on the requirements of the individual position. The specific internship description should be consulted before applying.

Are all the internships in the same field?

No. The current openings cover Human Resources, executive support, microfinance, climate, technology and finance.

Are the expired internships still included?

No. This updated article removes the four opportunities whose deadlines were August 18, August 19 and August 20, 2026.

Conclusion

The BRAC Regular Internship 2026 programme currently offers several opportunities for students, graduates and early-career candidates to gain practical experience in areas ranging from human resources and executive support to microfinance, climate action, information technology and finance.

The most important step is to identify an internship that genuinely matches your academic background and career objectives, read its official description carefully, confirm the location and eligibility requirements, and submit a complete application before the relevant deadline.

For the latest information and official application instructions, applicants should consult BRAC’s official Regular Internship page and the individual internship descriptions provided above.
